scenes.intro: Hello Timothy and Melanie. Your financial health score is 60 out of 100, which Sherpas calls stable. You are about to see your plan drawn as your own home, with each part showing what is solid and what needs work.
scenes.pillar_savings_and_cash_flow: Your plumbing is solid, at 26 out of 30 points. You hold $150,800 in cash, well above the reserve that covers emergencies. Education is the main open goal, and meeting it would take more saving each year.
scenes.pillar_debt: Your walls are cracked, at 12 out of 20 points. Most debt is manageable, but the $18,000 card at 18% is the costly part. At $300 a month, it is projected to be paid off in September 2039, so it can sit with you for years.
scenes.pillar_investments: Your garden is cracked, at 8 out of 15 points. You hold $150,000 in cash against $210,000 in invested savings, so a lot of your money is not set up to grow. Your mix is 81.2% stocks against a 98.0% target, which can mean slower growth for retirement.
scenes.pillar_liquidity_and_emergency_fund: Your foundations are solid, at 15 out of 15 points. You hold $150,801 in accessible cash, about 16 months of essentials, well above the 8 to 9 months recommended. Even after a $6,000 vacation, your cushion still stands.
scenes.pillar_insurance_and_protection: Your roof is broken, at 7 out of 20 points. Timothy has $140,000 of life cover against a recommended $750,000, a $610,000 gap, and Melanie is $490,000 short. You have no umbrella cover, the extra protection behind home and car insurance, so a $1,000,000 liability claim is uncovered. That leaves your children and savings open to real harm.
scenes.move_1: Your plan already includes paying $6,800 on the 18% card from cash. It repairs the walls by clearing the costly card balance, and lifts your score from 60 out of 100 to 62 out of 100.
scenes.move_2: Your plan already includes adding $235,000 of life cover. It repairs the roof by closing part of the gap, though on its own your score stays at 60 out of 100.
scenes.move_3: Your plan already includes adding $1M of umbrella cover, the extra protection behind your home and car insurance. It repairs the roof, and on its own your score stays at 60 out of 100.
scenes.all_moves: Together, the plan's steps pay down the high interest card, add life cover and add umbrella cover. As a group, they lift your score from 60 out of 100 to 78 out of 100.
scenes.timeline: Looking ahead, Timothy plans to retire at 62 and Melanie at 60. The plan has your debts paid off by 2059, and your savings and investments last all the way through. You are projected to still have $2,371,901 in today's dollars, a cushion if later years cost more than expected.
